name: Repair and heal allies
summary: A unit restores teammates' health in the field instead of, or as well as, fighting: a mechanic's tool or a repair beam held on a damaged vehicle, a medic's touch or healing beam on a soldier, or an aura or crane that mends everything near it. It saves the trip back to a repair building and is often free, but a big repair takes time. The repairer is usually fragile and unarmed or lightly armed, has to stay close behind the allies it mends and within reach of its patient, and so becomes the enemy's first target. Variants charge money or materials for each repair, mend only machines or only people, remove harmful effects such as parasites or toxins, boost the ally instead of healing it, or bring fallen teammates back.
counterplay: Kill the repairer first: it is usually fragile and unarmed, and once it falls its patient starts losing ground again.
Out-damage the repair: burst the patient faster than it is mended, or finish it before the repairer arrives.
Break the link: drive the patient and the repairer apart, since the repair stops once they are out of reach.
Splash the pair: the repairer stands right next to the ally it is mending.
Keep up the pressure: where the tool overheats or drains money, the repair can't run forever.
Attack what it can't fix: a vehicle mechanic can't heal soldiers, and a medic can't mend tanks.

other_examples.note: The mechanic's infantry twin: a slow, unarmed soldier who heals friendly infantry near him on his own, a little at a time until they are whole. He can't treat his own wounds, so medics work best together.

sources.title: Medic (Red Alert 1), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Its quote box copies the Red Alert manual entry.

other_examples.note: A passenger-set version: an Engineer riding in the IFV swaps its missiles for a repair crane that fixes damaged vehicles near it, fast and at no cost, so tanks can be mended at the front.

sources.title: Infantry Fighting Vehicle, Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Its quote box copies the Red Alert 2 manual entry.

other_examples.unit: Multigunner IFV with an engineer inside (Allies)
other_examples.note: Any side's engineer inside turns the car's launcher into a repair tool: it drives up to damaged friendly vehicles close by and mends them, and it also pulls Terror Drones out of infested hosts.

sources.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3/Multigunner IFV Infantry Effects, StrategyWiki

other_examples.note: A cheap, unarmed support car with a healing aura for infantry around it and, since a Zero Hour patch, for ground vehicles too. Infantry carried inside heal much faster, and it can also clean toxins and radiation off an area.

The US army's only repair unit: a small, poorly armed squad that brings damaged vehicles and buildings back to full health at an average rate while slightly draining manpower income. The repair is cancelled if the patient moves too far away.

sources.title: Engineer Squad, Company of Heroes Wiki

other_examples.note: Workers repair any friendly mechanical unit, several of them on one target at once, and can be set to repair by themselves; the Medivac dropship heals infantry with a beam that uses up its energy.

Builders repair whatever they are told to assist, but the repair costs resources in proportion to the missing health, close to the price of rebuilding it. The patient can keep moving and firing, and leaving the builder's range cancels the repair.

shooter_analogues.note: A blowtorch gadget that mends friendly or empty vehicles and hurts enemy vehicles and soldiers. It overheats with use, and in Battlefield 3 passengers of unarmoured transports and some helicopters can repair their own ride on the move and earn points for it.

A beam held on a teammate that heals them, and heals much faster once they have gone a short while without being hurt, which rewards falling back to the medic. Its charge makes the medic and the patient briefly invulnerable.

shooter_analogues.unit: Nano-Armor Kit (Engineer) and Medical Applicator (Combat Medic)
shooter_analogues.note: Engineers hold fire to repair allied vehicles, power-armoured soldiers and deployables on a heat meter that overheats, but never the vehicle they are riding in, and they aim to defuse enemy mines; medics tether a beam to heal soldiers or to revive fallen ones.

sources.title: Nano-Armor Kit, PlanetSide 2 Wiki

sources.title: Medical Applicator, PlanetSide 2 Wiki
sources.note: Its WeaponInfobox Description field copies the game's own item description (official text; Daybreak's Census item collection).

shooter_analogues.note: Hold fire to keep a healing beam on one ally, which stays linked for a moment even out of sight, or hold the other button for a beam that raises the ally's damage instead; she can also bring a dead teammate back after a short cast.
A soldier's hammer repairs vehicles and structures only while the soldier carries basic materials to put into them, so field repair depends on supply.

player_translation.summary: A support player who keeps teammates in the fight: hold a repair or healing beam on a damaged ally and it recovers without leaving the front. Fragile and lightly armed, the repairer lives just behind the line, and both teams fight over it.
as_user: You buy a fragile support unit whose main tool is a repair or healing beam: hold left mouse on a damaged teammate (vehicles or soldiers, depending on the tool) to restore health, and score points for every bit you restore.
Positioning is the skill: stay close behind the armour you mend, out of the enemy's sight lines, and break off when they focus you.
You choose the patient: the tank taking fire up front, or the one that can pull back to you. Big repairs take time, so a patient that disengages gets fixed faster.
Your tool overheats, or in some variants costs team money for each repair, so you decide when it is worth spending.
as_target: Every repairer is a priority target: it is fragile, and its patient starts losing again once it falls.
Burst the patient faster than the beam mends it, or split the pair apart, since the beam drops at its range limit.
Read the beam: its colour and the green numbers on the patient show who is being kept alive.
teammates: Drivers protect their mechanic and stay inside its range, and the mechanic follows armoured pushes.
A natural protector pair: repairers make tanks last, and tanks shield repairers.
Where the tool allows it, repairing also pulls infesters off a vehicle, the standard answer to infest-vehicle.
On the enemy side, flankers and snipers get a clear job: hunt the repairer.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; hold left mouse to beam the friendly unit under the cursor (it snaps to the nearest ally in a small cone), within a short range ring.
Variants put their key on Q: drop a repair station, pulse an aura, or swap to a boost beam.
Middle mouse, the universal ping: patients call 'need repair' and repairers answer 'on my way'.
The tool never works on yourself; healing yourself is a different pattern.
feedback: A team-coloured beam with sparks on vehicles or crosses on soldiers, and green numbers on the patient.
Damaged allies show a wrench or cross icon to repairers, on screen and on the minimap.
The patient's HUD names who is repairing it; the repairer's crosshair shows the patient's health as a ring.
Clear start and stop sounds for the beam, and a heat meter in the repairer's HUD.
changes_from_rts: The Red Alert 1 mechanic walks to damaged vehicles by himself; here a player picks patients and aims the tool, so it needs a forgiving snap to moving targets.
RTS field repair is often free and unlimited; a heat meter, a small cost or a slower rate under fire stops one repairer from making a tank unkillable.
Red Alert 1 splits the job between the mechanic (vehicles) and the medic (soldiers); separate tools by target type give clear roles, or one slower tool can do both.
Give score and assist credit for health restored, or few players will choose support.
Block self-use, and endless loops of repairers mending each other.

team_play.notes: Repairers make armour last and armour shields repairers; the enemy has to coordinate to kill the repairer first or burst through the healing, and tools that pull off infesters give the team a rescue.

notes: A beam that restores health on allies is simple; filtering patients by class (vehicles or soldiers) is a small rule.
Heat or cost rules, a range ring, and score for healing.
Cues for damaged allies and active beams, and a snap-to-target that copes with moving vehicles.
Interactions with other systems: removing infesters, clearing other effects, reviving.
Pocket healing can make one ally nearly unkillable; cap it with heat, a slower rate under fire, and no stacking of several beams at full rate.
Several repairers on one patient multiply its staying power.
Too weak, or unrewarded, and nobody plays it.
Beams read well from above, but enemies must see who is being healed and how fast, or the patient's health bar seems to lie.
Several overlapping beams in a brawl are hard to follow.

variants.name: Repair beam
variants.summary: Hold a beam or tool on one ally to restore its health; some versions overheat with use (Battlefield repair tool, PlanetSide 2 Nano-Armor Kit).
variants.seen_in: Battlefield repair tool, PlanetSide 2 Nano-Armor Kit, Team Fortress 2 Medi Gun, Overwatch Mercy

variants.name: Hands-on fix
variants.summary: Touching range only: the repairer has to stand right beside the patient, which is slow and exposed but strong.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 Field Mechanic and his socket wrench; Company of Heroes engineers

variants.name: Healing aura
variants.summary: Heals every friendly unit nearby, slowly and by itself; riders carried inside heal faster.

variants.name: Paid repair
variants.summary: Each repair spends team money or materials the repairer carries, so saving units costs economy.
variants.seen_in: Supreme Commander repair; Foxhole hammer; Company of Heroes engineers (a small income drain)

adds_weaknesses.why: Every repair spends team money or carried materials, so it can't keep mending forever.

variants.name: Faster when safe
variants.summary: Repair is slow on an ally under fire and fast on one that has pulled back, so retreating to the repairer pays.

variants.name: Repair and cleanse
variants.summary: The tool also removes harmful effects: parasites or infesters latched on, toxins on the ground, or enemy mines.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 3 Multigunner IFV with an engineer (removes Terror Drones); Generals Ambulance (cleans toxins); PlanetSide 2 Nano-Armor Kit (defuses mines)

variants.name: Heal or boost
variants.summary: The same beam can heal the ally or raise its damage instead, never both, so the support chooses between staying power and firepower.

variants.name: Revive the fallen
variants.summary: Fallen teammates can be brought back on the spot after a short channel, instead of going back to the buy screen.

adds_strengths.why: Keeps teammates fighting at the front by mending them in the field instead of sending them back to base.

adds_weaknesses.why: Its tool does little or nothing to enemies, so it is weak in a fight and has to stay close behind the allies it mends.

counters.why: Its repair pulls infesters out of their host, as repair does against Terror Drones in Red Alert 2 and 3.

countered_by.why: Snipers pick off the fragile repairer standing behind the line.
Flankers reach the support player at the back and kill it before it can run.
Splash hits the repairer standing next to its patient.

open_questions: One tool for vehicles and soldiers, or separate tools as in Red Alert 1 (the mechanic and the medic)?
Should repairs cost team money or carried materials (Supreme Commander, Foxhole), or only heat?
Should the repair tool also pull off infesters and clear other effects, and is reviving fallen teammates part of the support kit?
How much score for health restored, so that support is a rewarding pick?

shooter_fit.reason: The best-proven support job in team shooters (Battlefield engineers, TF2 medics, PlanetSide 2 engineers): a beam on an ally reads well from above and creates clear protect-the-healer and hunt-the-healer play.
